reference_review: Original turnaround, T-pose drawings and three earlier render sheets supplied in chat. Earlier editable meshes were not present, so no donor geometry was retained.
geometry_inspection: Final texture-free head: front, profile, elevated three-quarter
Final full body: front, profile, back and three-quarter, same orthographic scale
Large three-quarter head and elevated back/crown view
Native left hand/watch and sneaker detail
Actual GLB imported into an empty Blender scene, welded with corner normals preserved, then rendered again
observations: Crown was lowered with underlying skull; the small cowlick is continuous with the crown rather than a detached fin.
Hair is one closed manifold mesh; broad directional relief is geometric and visible in untextured views.
No visible scalp breakthrough or loose hair pieces in inspected views. The nape is tidy and rear relief is restrained.
Glasses retain rectangular depth in three-quarter and profile views. No eye/frame collision observed in the reviewed images.
Short recessed neck meets the collar, with a defined underside of the jaw.
Raised sleeve corners and back-hem jean breakthrough were corrected and re-rendered. No remaining visible hem/sleeve clipping found in these views.
Hands have four fingers and a thumb, joined to the arm mesh. The left watch sits above the dorsal wrist.
Sneakers were rebuilt from wedge-like uppers to a lower toe box and instep, with uppers seated on the soles. Both feet touch the same ground plane.
Reimported GLB retains visible flat facets, palette and texture details.
remaining_limits: Facial expression is static; expression shapes and extreme joint bending were not tested because this pass has no rig.
Rear hair relief, stubble and painted shoe detail become subdued at small on-screen sizes; the major hair/glasses/clothing silhouette remains the main identity cue.
The native Blender 4.3.2 file is not a 2.93-native save; GLB and the optional import helper are supplied, but 2.93 execution remains untested.
artist_approval: pending; technical checks do not imply user design approval
